## The defect (F-506/F-518, L2-M07)

A `sig.connector.subject` value must name exactly one real subject
(§3.1). Upstream, key derivation was an incidental concat of whatever the
emitter held — and the composed fields were not unique: camera keys folded
**5,278** real cameras onto collided keys (the plan row's count — re-derived
at run time, never assumed); `atlas:`/EFF agency strings merged across
states; `contract:` external ids merged across tenants (legistar/civicclerk/
primegov share the id space); `data_driven:agency:` collided across releases.
The spine's model forbids a rewrite — the fix is a **declared grammar** plus
**append-only correction**, not an UPDATE.

## What ships

- **The pin registry — `db/src/db/data/subject_key_pins.toml`
  (`sig.subject-key-pins/1`).** Per family: ordered `fields`, the
  `scope` rendering (`kind = "scheme_prefixed"` — the scope renders as TWO
  segments, literal scheme token + value, so current and legacy values are
  disjoint by construction; `absent ∈ unscoped|omit`), `legacy_fields`
  arities that still parse (never minted — including the slug-shaped seed
  convention), the `distinguish` selectors the collision scan re-derives,
  and the `split` shape. `db/src/db/subject_keys.py` is the single
  implementation: `mint_subject_key`, `parse_subject_key`,
  `split_subject_key`, `validate_subject_value`, `assert_unique_within` —
  a segment containing `:` mints fail closed so positional parsing stays
  unambiguous.
- **Emitters on one derivation.** `atlas.py` and `data_driven.py` gain
  `us.state_abbr:<state>` (`absent` → `unscoped`); `procurement.py`
  `contract:` gains `tenant:<tenant_id>` (`absent` → omit, single-tenant
  keeps the legacy shape) and the pre-existing `agenda_item:`/
  `agenda_document:` convention mints through the declared pins;
  `dot_511.py` cameras keep the `traffic_camera:` anchor (≈232k existing
  subjects — a scheme change would fork them into permanent append-only
  twins) minted through the same function.
- **GQ-04's I-placement.** `dot_511` collects every minted key per capture
  and `assert_unique_within` aborts the target run with
  `SubjectKeyCollision` when two upstream rows mint one key — the F-518
  defect class can never re-enter. `claim_sink` additionally validates
  every stored pinned-family value against the grammar
  (`validate_subject_value`); drift quarantines with
  `unknown_subject_scheme`-class rejection. Unpinned families pass through
  — the registry is deliberately partial.
- **The append-only re-key run — `db/src/db/subject_rekey.py` +
  `sig-db subject-rekey` (plan by default, `--apply` writes, `--limit`
  bounds).** `collision_scan` re-derives collided keys LIVE via each pin's
  `distinguish` selectors; `plan_subject` groups current claims into
  per-upstream-record evidence bundles (`capture_id` + locator) and
  clusters them by the pin's discriminator — camera bundles on their
  coordinate pair (`:s<n>` constituent suffix — a truthful upstream ref is
  never guessed), scoped families on the evidenced scope value
  (`raw_context`). `apply_subject` runs one transaction per key
  (resumable): each moved claim closes (`sys_period` end — the only UPDATE
  the run issues) and appends under the guard-minted constituent entity
  with `revises_claim` + `correction_reason='subject_rekey_constituent'` +
  an identity-class `content_digest` (P35.22/ADR-211); every
  `claim_evidence` row re-binds verbatim. One `subject_rekey_decision` per
  (old value, constituent) records discriminator + counts + run + registry
  version — `UNIQUE (scheme, old_value, new_value, registry_version)` makes
  a rerun +0; decision + pin rows are immutable by trigger. Claims whose
  bundle carries no discriminator stay on the legacy key — `unplaced`,
  reported, never guessed.
- **Sqitch `subject_rekey`** — `subject_key_pin` (registry mirror, seeds
  pinned by test parity), `subject_rekey_decision` (append-only log, FK
  into `entity_identity_key`), `claim_evidence(claim_id)` index. Deploy →
  verify → revert → redeploy all green in the whole-plan round-trip.
- **ADR-212** — the decisions and recorded deviations: `:s<n>` suffixes
  (never a guessed upstream ref), the `subject_rekey_constituent` reason
  string, `entity_identity_key` vs `entity_identifier` in scans, the
  pin-table-as-mirror posture, and why GQ-04 gets no spine evaluator (its
  placement is `I`).

## Boundaries

No hosted re-key run, no `/status/` post, no live collision verification
(queued — OM-20 conditional). No `UPDATE`/`DELETE` beyond the permitted
`sys_period` close; old bindings stay in history. No `ingestion_permitted`
flip, no HG gate tick, no merge/tag/`main` push, no living-record pins.
Schema delta is one additive sqitch change; stored keys are never
rewritten — a `contract:`-family value that parses legacy stays readable,
only minting changes.
